_comment: Single source of truth for which model and effort each skill and routine runs at. The runner reads this to build claude -p invocations; the dashboard Skills Deck renders cards straight from it. Prose policy for agents lives in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and pstack-models.md.

policy.why: Haiku is never used. Effort above high overthinks per step and produces bloated diffs at higher cost. The source video's XHIGH values are out of policy and must not be copied in.
policy.tie_break: When axes conflict for anything that ships: intelligence, then taste, then cost.

defaults.why: Opus is abundant on the Pro plan and handles clear-spec work unsupervised.
defaults.applies_to: Every skill and routine with no entry below. This file records deviations, not an inventory: 6 of the 70 installed skills have an entry and the other 64 run at these defaults. Absence means default, never 'helm does not run this'.

resume-tailor.why: Writes as Daniel for outside readers. Taste and voice matter more than speed.

know-it.why: Deep codebase analysis feeding interview preparation. Wrong depth here wastes hours of study.

update-vault.why: Mechanical: run a scanner, diff against notes, report drift.

impeccable.why: User-facing design needs taste at the top of the scale.

deep-review.why: Review work, per the standing model policy.

research.why: Reading legwork against primary sources. Volume over subtlety.

integrity-check.does: Runs helm's test suites and checks that the routers' pointers, the vault's wikilinks, the project notes, capture's sources and the services are all still sound. When something fails, Claude writes a short report naming what to fix in Inbox/runs/integrity and commits it to the vault.
integrity-check.why: Verifying that paths exist is close to mechanical. Runs every day, so cost compounds.

capture.does: Rebuilds the agenda and project snapshots the dashboard reads: open ideas and routine fires from the vault, and each project's git and GitHub state.
capture.why: Deterministic producers. Reading a note and reading git is not a judgment task; HELM measured 689 of 712 headless Claude runs reproducing a deterministic transform (HELM ADR 0008).
capture.writes: ~/.helm/status/agenda.json (open ideas, routine fires) and projects.json every run

doorbook-listings.does: Rereads the online listing of every house Doorbook marked for sale and records whether it is still on the market or has sold.
doorbook-listings.why: Reading a listing page for its status is a parse, not a judgment. Owned by the doorbook project, which keeps the code in scripts/listings; helm runs it before the work day so a house that sold overnight is on the phone by the first knock.

doorbook-market.does: Sweeps every listing in Doorbook's area, for sale, under contract and sold, with its listing agent and brokerage, for the realtor list.
doorbook-market.why: Reading listing pages for stage, dates and agent is a parse, not a judgment. Owned by the doorbook project, which keeps the code in scripts/market; helm runs it early each morning, before the listings check.

doorbook-debrief.does: Writes the evening debrief the Doorbook app shows: three things that worked that day, one thing to try tomorrow, and the best opener once pitch metrics exist.
doorbook-debrief.why: Coaching from a day's log is a judgment over a short printout, and it is Doorbook's one AI step; the calendar sync and the listings stay plain code. Sonnet at medium is enough for three sentences from a few hundred lines and it runs every work evening, so cost compounds. It runs every evening at 21:00, after the 19:30 end of every work day, and a day off has no knocks and writes nothing. Owned by the doorbook project (scripts/debrief).

backup.does: Copies the vault (a verified git bundle and a tarball of the working tree) and the state worth keeping to the backup drive. Skips when the drive is absent and sends one notification once the last good copy is 14 days old.
backup.why: The vault has no remote, so a local snapshot is its only copy. Pure code: a git bundle, two tarballs and a timestamp. It runs whenever a volume mounts and does nothing unless the backup drive is the one that appeared.

job-search.run: By hand: runner/routines/job-search.sh. Never scheduled, so install-routines.sh, alerts and the Background tab do not know it.
job-search.why: Ranking the live pool is a judgment call over up to sixty full postings and their verdicts, with the right to overturn a cheaper pass, so it runs at the top of the scale; the two passes before it have their own entries below, and the ten tailorings that follow run the resume-tailor skill at its own entry.

eligibility.why: Three facts read off each posting into a fixed form, a batch of postings per call. Sonnet reads the whole text and the code decides the drop; the input is a hundred full postings a morning, which is where cost compounds.

skills.why: The years floor, the primary stack and each required skill against the owner's inventory, also a fixed form per posting, a batch per call. Same reasoning: the volume of text read, and the ranker re-checks the survivors at the top of the scale.

job-search.writes: ~/Desktop/Job Apps/Jobs <day>.pdf and ~/Desktop/Job Apps/Jobs <day>/, Atlas/Work/research/<day>-jobs-top-10.md and <day>-jobs-dropped.md and Atlas/Work/files/applications/<day>/ in the vault, a Work idea due that day in Atlas/Ideas/, and ~/.helm/status/job-search/ (the day's stage files and costs, the pool, the posting and verdict caches)

dashboard.does: Serves this dashboard on port 8642, to this Mac and the tailnet.
dashboard.why: The dashboard is only worth having if it is already answering. launchd starts it at login and restarts it if it exits, so nothing has to be remembered before looking at the day.

doorbook-sync.does: Answers the Doorbook phone app: takes in the houses it marks for sale and hands back what the listings routine found.
doorbook-sync.why: The phone sends the houses it marked for sale and reads back their listings whenever the For sale page opens, so the door has to be answering. Loopback only, fronted by tailscale serve on 8665. Owned by the doorbook project (scripts/listings/serve.py).

triage.does: Starts a Claude session when a routine fails, goes quiet or a service is down. The session finds the cause, fixes it, tests it, reruns the job and commits, and stops before anything hard to undo. At most one per alert a day and three a day in all, and only once ~/.helm/triage/enabled exists. ADR 0041.
triage.why: Diagnosing a broken job from its logs, its status and the commits since it last worked is judgment over unfamiliar code with nobody watching, so it runs at the top of the policy. It fires rarely, so cost does not compound.
